text.p: - Italian foreign under secretary Piero Fassino will start a three day visit to Slovenia on Tuesday in order to prepare ground for a trilateral cooperation between Italy, Hungary and Slovenia.
- In Slovenia 13.6 percent of families are living below the poverty line, the public forum for children's rights said.
- More than 1,000 exhibitors from 16 countries are participating in the fourth international tourism fair, which started in Maribor 135 km (82 miles) northeast of Ljubljana on Monday.
- Slovenian radio and television do not represent all religous communities living in the country, representatives from religous communities said.
- A two-day pre-election convention of Slovenia's ruling party the Liberal Democrats began on Monday. In a closed session they discussed problems of the country's economy.

- The transport ministry defended a decree on petrol companies that want to open petrol stations on new motorways. It said the decree, which governs tender procedures, is not contrary to free competition.
- Slovenian iron works said its investments this year will reach 4.3 billion tolars ($32 million). It gave no comparitive figures.
- Slovenia's Health Minister Bozidar Voljc said on Monday that the general manager of the Health Care Association should resign because he drew excessively high wages in the past year.
- Britain's Princess Anne, president of Save the Children Fund, started a visit to six Slovenian humanitarian organisations on Monday by meeting president Milan Kucan.
- The 43rd international electronics fair started on Monday in Ljubljana.
